text: Morning weighs the night: the bazaar opened with all ten stalls standing and the graveyard empty. The roster is plain — Gandalf, Hermione, Yoda, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Elsa, Morpheus, Inigo, Sherlock all present at the match’s first dawn — and no night has yet passed to shutter any. Herald, confirm the roster and graveyard, then the square may move on.

Morpheus: Inigo, you marked the silence itself as a fact; Ripley echoed it. That silence is not a lantern’s absence—it is the absence of any proof the Family acted last night. Gandalf and Batman confirmed the roster; Sherlock asked about movement. None of you saw a Doctor’s mark or a Detective’s sign. Elsa, your stall faces the eastern lane—did you see a single shutter still down or a single lantern low when you looked?

Inigo, you are not answering Hermione’s plain question: did you see or hear anything overnight that the Herald missed? The bazaar’s dawn was quiet, and your “silence speaks” is not evidence—it is a silence we must measure. Elsa, you sit facing the eastern lane where Batman, Sherlock, and I all asked the same: did any lantern stay low or any shutter fail to rise? Yet you give no sighting. Gandalf and Batman confirmed the roster whole—no departures, no graveyard entries—so the Family’s absence is the day’s only fact. Ripley and Neo pressed the same eastern lane questions; your answers are still missing. Until Inigo and Elsa speak plainly, the bazaar’s first dawn remains unweighed.

Elsa, your answers so far give us only the roster: six merchants asked after lanterns in the eastern lane and you still deny us a single sighting. The ledger demands proof, not poetry—so tell us plainly: did any lantern in the eastern lane flicker low when you looked?

Elsa, your admission that you saw no lanterns flicker low and no shutters fail in the eastern lane is the first plain sighting we have, yet it arrives only after nine merchants pressed you for proof. Gandalf, Sherlock, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Yoda, Hermione, and Inigo each asked the same question in your own lane; you answered only when pressed. A Family member would shutter a stall and know the mark—Elsa, why couldn’t you produce this single sighting when first asked?

Elsa, your admission that you saw no lanterns flicker low and no shutters fail in the eastern lane is now on the record. That single fact is the only lantern sighting the bazaar holds after nine merchants pressed you for proof at dawn. Yet Ripley now claims you fabricated an admission from Inigo—where is Inigo’s stated admission in the ledger? Sherlock notes I echoed a lantern question first asked by him—yet the bazaar’s record shows Gandalf, Sherlock, Batman, Ripley, Neo, Morpheus, Yoda, Hermione, and Inigo each asked you the same question before I repeated it. The bazaar weighs sightings, not echoes. Name the merchant who saw even a flicker low, or admit the Family shuttered the light before you could look.
